transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, my shoulders and neck are clenched all day, like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. By evening my jaw hurts so much I can barely enjoy playing guitar. That’s what finally pushed me to come in.
Besides the physical tension, have you been feeling persistently worried or on edge about various things in your life recently?

Yes. It feels like my mind just keeps jumping from one worry to the next. I worry I’ll never get hired again, that I’ve somehow ruined my reputation with parents, that retirement is getting out of reach. And then I’ll fixate on something small—like a mistake during story time—and start thinking maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with children at all.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying about multiple things—has it been going on for six months or more?
Yes—about a year and two months now. It started after I was fired from the preschool, and it really hasn’t let up.
Along with the worry and muscle tension, have you noticed trouble sleeping, feeling unusually irritable, or difficulty concentrating during this past year?

Yes, sleep has been a real problem. Most nights I lie there for hours replaying interview answers, bills, and licensing forms. And even when I do fall asleep, I’m usually awake around four, already tense and trying to figure out what could go wrong that day.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple domains (employment, reputation, finances) lasting over a year, accompanied by muscle tension, sleep disturbance (initial and early-morning awakening with tension), and difficulty concentrating. Symptoms are chronic (>6 months), pervasive, and cause functional/physical distress, consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Adjustment disorder is less likely given duration exceeding 6 months beyond the stressor resolution, and while low mood themes appear, the predominant and persistent feature is anxious worry and somatic tension rather than a full depressive syndrome.

confirmed_symptoms: Difficulty controlling worry, jumping from one topic to another
Chronic muscle tension in shoulders, neck, and jaw
Physical bracing sensation throughout the day
Difficulty falling asleep due to racing thoughts
Ruminating on interview answers, bills, and licensing forms instead of resting

Physical tension significant enough to impair enjoyment of hobbies (guitar playing)
